assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, universal statistical-physics mechanism: Vicsek's minimal self-propelled-particle model showed a flocking transition, and Toner-Tu hydrodynamics showed that long-range orientational order survives in two dimensions, beyond Mermin-Wagner. Ramaswamy's hydrodynamics of active polar and nematic fluids supplied the generic framework. This is a new branch of nonequilibrium statistical physics with a simple essential mechanism, spanning bacteria, cell layers, bird flocks and synthetic active colloids.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek for the model and numerical discovery, Toner (with Tu) for the hydrodynamic theory and the exact scaling picture, Ramaswamy for the active-fluid hydrodynamic framework and active-matter theory. The three names give a natural prize; Yuhai Tu is not in the credited list, which is a real attribution gap I cannot repair here.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation: numerical, theoretical (renormalisation group) and experiments on bacterial turbulence, colloidal rollers and vibrated granular matter. The giant number fluctuations and flocking scaling are reasonably well established, although quantitative agreement with the Toner-Tu exponents in experiments is still partly debated. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Absence of Yuhai Tu from the credited names complicates fair credit for the Toner-Tu theory.
Experimental tests of the exact scaling exponents are limited; the committee may regard the field as broad rather than a single decisive discovery.
I rely on my own recollection of the priority between Vicsek, Toner-Tu and Ramaswamy and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle (Bistritzer-MacDonald), followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum materials, a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Prediction and experiment form a clean, mutually reinforcing pair, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments (with Cao and others). Cao Yuan is not among the credited names, so the experimental side rests on Jarillo-Herrero as group leader. Three-person configuration works well, though Kim, Dean, Efetov and others contributed to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups, with fractional Chern insulators and related phases following. The field is young (2018) and the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism remains unsettled, but the original discovery is robust. Timely rather than premature, though some committee members may prefer to wait.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and nature of the correlated states are not settled.
Credit of the experimental discovery depends on junior researchers not in the credited list.
Whether the field's long-term impact is yet clear enough for a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and E91) turned entanglement and the no-cloning principle into a practical cryptographic primitive, tying fundamental quantum foundations to technology. The ideas are simple, general and have driven a large experimental effort including satellite links. The 2022 prize recognised related Bell-test physics, so this is a natural continuation.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard for BB84, Ekert for the entanglement-based protocol; this is a well-defined trio. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea and the Bennett-Brassard-Mermin work on E91 equivalence may raise priority questions that I cannot resolve from memory.
assessment.maturity: Strong: protocols proven secure, widely demonstrated experimentally, with commercial and national-scale networks. Practical security against side-channel attacks is a continuing issue but does not affect the originality of the discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as physics rather than information science.
Priority issues around Wiesner and related earlier ideas.
Overlap with other quantum-information candidates on the longlist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells: P granules and nucleoli behaving as liquid droplets, with the theoretical framework from soft-matter physics. This brings statistical physics and polymer theory into cell biology in a way that matches the interdisciplinary cross-fertilisation I value, with a clear underlying mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne for the experimental demonstration in 2009; Jülicher for the active-droplet theory. The three names give a coherent configuration. Other contributors (Rosen, Rosen-type work on multivalent proteins, Tanaka and others) are outside the credited list, and attribution against them could be contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly widened since 2009; the physical picture is widely accepted for many condensates but debates continue about how universally liquid-like behaviour applies in vivo, and about artefacts of overexpression. Possibly premature as a physics prize and more suited to chemistry or medicine.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance versus in vitro droplets and overexpression artefacts.
Whether the discovery is mainly biology and so outside the physics prize remit.
Credit relative to other contributors outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems (Evans-Searles, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski equality, Crooks) are exact results for nonequilibrium systems that generalise the second law and relate work distributions to free-energy differences. They are conceptually clean, general and have shaped single-molecule biophysics and stochastic thermodynamics. This is close to my own field of stochastic processes.
assessment.attribution: The attribution is the weakest feature: Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski, Crooks, Kurchan and Lebowitz-Spohn all contributed key results, so any three names omit major contributors. Crooks is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified (RNA hairpin pulling, Wang et al. colloidal tests, quantum-system tests) and thoroughly mathematised. The result is mature, although in mathematical physics terms it has arguably been absorbed into the standard toolkit.
uncertainties: Large and contested credit allocation that a three-person prize cannot fairly resolve.
Whether the concrete discovery is a single identifiable one.
Experimental impact, though real, is mostly in biophysics and small systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations of record precision, reach fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and are paving the way for redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. Both the idea and the experimental realisation are clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the first clocks; Jun Ye brought the clocks to the leading precision and into many applications. Two laureates fit well. Hall and Hansch were already recognised in 2005 for the frequency comb that these clocks depend on. Contributions from Ludlow, Hinkley and others and from ion-clock groups (Wineland already prized) are acknowledged elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with numerous independent confirmations and redefinition of the SI second under discussion. Timing is good, though it is close in spirit to previous metrology prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion cooling may reduce perceived novelty.
Whether it is a single discovery or a long incremental improvement.
Ion-clock and Sr-lattice groups other than the credited two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and its observation in HgTe quantum wells launched topological insulators, a major conceptual development that connected band topology with robust edge transport. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions in the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz tradition, but this later development is distinct and well established.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele for the Z2 theory; Molenkamp for the experimental realisation in HgTe (with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Konig). Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang (deceased 2018) are not in this credited set, which is a real credit problem; the dual ballot B010 gives an alternative configuration I have not used.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with many independent experiments, three-dimensional topological insulators, and the many spinoffs. Timing is no longer premature; the risk is that other topological candidates are competing.
uncertainties: Missing credit to Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and to the 3D topological insulator discoverers.
Competing and overlapping topological candidates elsewhere on the longlist.
Part of the field may have been implicitly covered by the 2016 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models, shown by the superfluid-Mott insulator transition (Greiner et al.) after the Jaksch-Zoller proposal, and now serve as quantum simulators of many-body physics. The idea of programmable analog simulation of statistical models is attractive to a theorist.
assessment.attribution: The configuration limits laureates to three of Bloch, Cirac, Greiner, Zoller. Zoller and Bloch (with Greiner as the experimental discoverer and Hansch as co-author) is a natural trio, but Jaksch is not credited, and Cirac's role overlaps with the trapped-ion and atomic-quantum-computation entries elsewhere. I propose three with the least overlap.
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated worldwide, with quantum gas microscopes and quantitative simulations; however, quantum simulation is still developing toward answering questions beyond classical reach, and the overlap with Bose-Einstein condensation prizes is notable.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among four names plus the uncredited Jaksch.
Overlap with other atomic quantum-information candidates on the list.
Whether quantum simulation has yet produced a decisive new discovery.
